body: I'm experiencing a similar issue with the edge runtime enabled in app router. With edge runtime disabled the url params that are returned to the page look like `['path-1', 'path-2']`. With edge runtime enabled, the array gets concatenated into a url encoded single string `['path-1%2Fpath-2']`. Any help is appreciated.

Is it by design? 

According to source code: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f19b31ad93c313cb86d9a589c931f8f9718a7fb2/packages/next/src/client/components/navigation.ts#L148

And test case:
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f19b31ad93c313cb86d9a589c931f8f9718a7fb2/test/e2e/app-dir/use-params/use-params.test.ts#L36

Currently, `useParams()` will only return `string`, there is no return `array` logic.

Should we add return `array` logic?
Locally (using dev server) a string array is returned correctly. But once deployed to an instance with edge runtime, the string array gets concatenated into an array with just 1 string.

In my local environment, I am encountering a similar issue with the `useParams` hook. When using the `catch-all` route, the value returned by `useParams` for the catch-all route is a `string` instead of an `array`. However, I have not yet tested this behavior on Vercel with the edge runtime.

After examining the code for the `useParams` function, I found that its returned value is an object where each value is a `string`. 

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/f19b31ad93c313cb86d9a589c931f8f9718a7fb2/packages/next/src/client/components/navigation.ts#L129-L131

However, I am puzzled because the [documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-params#returns) states that returned value can have both `string` or `string[]`.

issue.title: Ensure useParams return array for catch-all routes
issue.body:

Ensures `useParams` matches `params` passed to the page, also matches the docs.

Fixes #50856

### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

_No response_

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue or a replay of the bug

https://github.com/remorses/next.js-bug-encoded-dynamic-param/tree/main

### To Reproduce

-   Deploy to Vercel with `edge` runtime
-   click the link `navigate to another/random`
-   Notice that the param `slug` is not an array of paths, but it's url encoded (something like `["another%2Frandom"]`)

### Describe the Bug

The catch all param `slug` is not an array of paths, but it's an array of a string url encoded (something like `["another%2Frandom"]`)

### Expected Behavior

`slug` should be `["another", "random"]


Related to 
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/50856
https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/47651 (that was when using `experimental-edge`, the slash was not url encoded)
https://github.com/vercel/vercel/issues/9723


### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

Not relevant

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

Vercel
